title: A 938-turn coding session
result: One coding trace that exceeded 800k tokens of context was replayed for 938 turns. At Sonnet rates the estimated model cost went from $154 to $43, a reported 72.3% reduction.
caveat: One unusually long trace. Helene 1 and Adeline 1 ran live; model costs were priced from cache-tier usage at Anthropic list rates. The Sonnet and Opus rows are the same session.

title: Where long sessions spend their tokens
result: Across 12 coding sessions and 18,333 assistant turns, cache reads accounted for 67.7% of the baseline model cost.
caveat: A breakdown of the sampled workload, not a savings percentage or a separate compression trial.

title: RTK on Terminal-Bench
result: In one Terminal-Bench comparison, cost per suite pass rose from $25.46 without RTK to $29.33 with RTK (+15.2%).
caveat: No Condense arm. One run per setting; task outcomes vary across repeats. This measures suite cost rather than shell-output compression.

title: Helene 1.1 on Lost in Compression
result: At the roughly 50%-text-retained band, Helene 1.1 scored 7.09 accuracy points above bear-2 on the multilingual QA comparison.
caveat: 3,000 paired items across ten languages. Retained-text rates were approximately matched: Helene kept 1.02 percentage points more text than bear-2 at this band. This measures answer accuracy, not coding-agent solve rate.

title: Helene 1 on CoQA
result: Across 150 CoQA turns, auto mode removed 30.6% of input tokens and scored 92.0% judged accuracy, versus 90.0% on uncompressed text.
caveat: GPT-5.4 answered and judged the same 150 turns. The observed two-point difference represents three answers; no statistical significance is established.

title: Helene 1 on LongBench v2
result: On 150 LongBench v2 items, Helene 1 auto removed 38.8% of 15.7M input tokens. Measured accuracy was 49.3%, versus 48.7% on uncompressed text.
caveat: One sample, one answerer/judge pairing. The accuracy difference is approximately one item. The separate 50-item code/structured-data figure is a subset of this test.

title: Adeline 1 on CoderForge SWE traces
result: On held-out CoderForge coding traces, Adeline 1 retained 94.2% of atomic facts while removing 90.2% of Claude-token input.
caveat: Inputs were 30k–100k tokens. Fact recall measures information retained in compacted traces, not task completion or a reduction in model cost.

title: Axiometa Studio
result: Median cost per Studio turn, including failed turns, went from $0.45 to $0.16. Axiometa reports a 65% reduction.
caveat: Before/after customer deployment combining compression, managed caching and changes to the agent workflow. The 65% cannot be attributed to compression alone.
